stemBlocks.value: (a) The determinant of the matrix (6  2v / -5  -v) is 24. Calculate the value of v. (b)(c) L = (9  5 / 3  2) and M = (2 / -4). Evaluate (i) the matrix product LM and (ii) L inverse.
Think first: Write the determinant out with its signs before simplifying; the two negatives combine to give a positive term.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p298-q09 from workbook page 298.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the determinant as leading diagonal product minus the other diagonal product.
Set the determinant equal to 24 and solve.
Multiply L by the column matrix M.
Swap the leading diagonal entries, change the signs of the other two, and divide by 3.

strategyBlocks.value: Expand the determinant in terms of v and solve, then multiply L by the column M and finish by finding det L and applying the inverse formula.

whyThisWorks.value: The determinant of a 2x2 matrix is always the product of the leading diagonal minus the product of the other diagonal, so an unknown entry turns it into a simple linear equation. The inverse of a 2x2 matrix is the adjugate, formed by swapping the leading diagonal and negating the other two entries, divided by the determinant; multiplying it back by the original returns the identity matrix, which is why the determinant must not be zero.
